## Control structures

### ifelse(test,yes,No)

```{r}
pvalues<-c(0.867,0.0054,0.0018,0.1572,0.0183,0.5386)
results<-ifelse(pvalues<0.05,"Significant","Not significant")
results

data2<-data.frame(pvalues,results)

View(data2)

```

```{r}
z< -5
set.seed(1)
while(z>=3 && z<=5){
  coin<-rbinom(1,1,0.5)
  if (coin==1){
    z=z+1
  } else {
    z<-z-1
  }
}


```

```{r}
# Create student dataset

students <- data.frame(
  Student_ID = 1:6,
  Name = c("John", "Mary", "Peter",
           "Alice", "David", "Grace"),
  Marks = c(85, 45, 67, 30, 90, 55)
)

# Display dataset
print(students)


marks <- 75

if (marks >= 60) {
  print("PASS")
}


marks <- 45

if (marks >= 60) {
  print("PASS")
} else {
  print("FAIL")
}



students$Decision <- ifelse(
  students$Marks >= 60,
  "PASS",
  "FAIL"
)

print(students)





for (i in 1:nrow(students)) {

  if (students$Marks[i] >= 60) {

    print(paste(
      students$Name[i],
      "Passed"
    ))

  } else {

    print(paste(
      students$Name[i],
      "Failed"
    ))
  }
}



i <- 1

while (i <= nrow(students)) {

  print(students$Name[i])

  i <- i + 1
}
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
